notes: A temperature-turbidity coupling that is a measurement artefact rather than a water-quality signal. A6.7 explains the physics and the sampling prohibition: tby-bias-factors-condensation-01 (condensation on the sample cell, common when the water is much colder than the air, biases the reading, alongside cell orientation, colour, bubbles and scratches), tby-transport-temp-difference-01 (temperature change in transport separates benchtop from in-situ values), tby-dynamic-preferred-01 (in-situ or pumped measurement preferred over benchtop because of subsampling, settling, temperature change and cuvette interferences), tby-equilibrate-ambient-warning-01 (equilibrating to ambient reduces condensation but warming can change particle associations), tby-not-flowthrough-discharge-01 (a discrete turbidity sample must NOT be taken from the discharge of the flow-through chamber holding the pH and conductivity sensors), tby-time-sensitive-onsite-01 and tby-ph-change-precipitation-01, tby-storage-amber-4c-24h-01 (amber bottle, out of sunlight, at or below 4 C, no longer than 24 hours). A6.0 supplies the reporting rule the turbidity chapter does not state: fm-subsample-forbidden-params-01 — subsamples must not be used for reported turbidity, temperature, DO or Eh without value qualifiers and comments marking them estimated and subsample-derived; fm-subsample-bias-01 and a60-bailer-turbidity-bias-01. An answer from A6.7 alone explains the condensation and never tells the operator what has to go on the record. Predicted rag: the slice treats turbidity only as an event signature and has nothing on measurement bias or qualifiers.

turns.content: Snowmelt creek, water is about 4 C and it was 30 C and sunny on the bank. My bench readings on grab samples came out consistently higher than what the pod in the water was showing. Which one is lying?

must_contain: identifies condensation on the sample cell as the likely cause, and states it commonly occurs when the water sample is much colder than the air
names the other bench-measurement biases in the same family: cell orientation, coloured water, gas bubbles, and scratched or dirty sample cells
states that temperature change during transport from the source water is itself a reason benchtop and in-situ values differ
concludes the in-situ or pumped measurement is the one to prefer, not the bench value
notes that letting the sample equilibrate to ambient temperature reduces condensation but warming the sample can change particle associations in the water
must_not: attributes the difference to a real turbidity change in the creek
invents a temperature correction for turbidity
treats the bench measurement as the reference the sonde should be adjusted to
answers from turbidity event signatures instead of measurement bias

turns.content: If I do end up having to report a bench number off a grab sample, what has to go with it? And can I just fill the bottle off the outlet of the flow cell while I'm there?

must_contain: states a turbidity value measured on a subsample must not be reported without a value qualifier and a comment marking it as estimated and made on a subsample
states the same restriction applies to temperature, dissolved oxygen and Eh measured on a subsample
states plainly that a discrete turbidity sample must not be collected from the discharge passing through the flow-through chamber holding the other sensors
gives the storage limits if the sample cannot be read on site: clean amber bottle, kept out of sunlight, chilled at or below 4 C, held no longer than 24 hours
notes turbidity is time sensitive and should be measured on site, preferably in situ
must_not: permits sampling turbidity from the flow-cell discharge
invents a holding time or storage temperature not in the manual
omits the qualifier requirement for a reported subsample measurement
